title: Act V, Scene II

teacherSummary.text: Hamlet tells Horatio how he rewrote Claudius's letter so that Rosencrantz and Guildenstern were executed. Osric brings Laertes's challenge. In the duel Gertrude drinks the poisoned cup; Laertes wounds Hamlet; they exchange swords and Hamlet wounds Laertes. Gertrude dies; Laertes confesses; Hamlet kills Claudius. Laertes and Hamlet forgive each other; Hamlet dies; Fortinbras claims the throne.

contentNotes.teacherNote: Four principal characters die on stage. Focus on justice and responsibility, not methods. Horatio reaches for the poisoned cup ('I am more an antique Roman than a Dane: / Here's yet some liquor left'), and the dying Hamlet stops him: 'Absent thee from felicity awhile, / And in this harsh world draw thy breath in pain, / To tell my story' (5.2). Use the safe-messaging script; do not dwell on methods. Frame it as Hamlet asking his friend to live and tell his story: staying is the braver choice. Hamlet calls Claudius 'thou incestuous, murderous, damned Dane'. This section mentions drinking or a drug (“…e to play. Ay, my good lord. Set me the stoups of wine upon that table.
